source_refs.note: Topic 23.5 (PDF 110-111); the equations are summarised in an original figure. The PCl3 equation follows the learning outcome; the printed 'CH2-COOH + NaHCO3' is read as CH3COOH. The reduction and oxidation definition boxes are not reproduced.

blocks.text: The reactions of carboxylic acids are of three types: those of the acidic hydrogen only, those that replace the -OH group, and those of the carboxyl group as a whole.
A. Reactions of the acidic hydrogen
Carboxylic acids are distinctly acidic because they give H+ ions in water, so they react with active metals, alkalis, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates:

items: With SOCl2, PCl3 or PCl5, acyl chlorides form: CH3COOH + SOCl2 -> CH3COCl + HCl + SO2; CH3COOH + PCl5 -> CH3COCl + HCl + POCl3; 3CH3COOH + PCl3 -> 3CH3COCl + H3PO3 (heat).
With alcohols (esterification), heating with concentrated sulphuric acid gives esters: CH3COOH + C2H5OH <=> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (ethyl ethanoate).

blocks.text: The powerful reducing agent lithium tetrahydridoaluminate(III), LiAlH4, reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols: CH3COOH + 4[H] -> CH3CH2OH + H2O. The common reducing agents H2/Ni and sodium tetrahydridoborate(III), NaBH4, do not reduce carboxylic acids.

Methanoic acid, HCOOH, is oxidised by both weak and strong oxidising agents, because its molecule contains an aldehyde-like part (H-C=O) as well as the carboxyl part; it is therefore a strong reducing agent. It is the only monocarboxylic acid that gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent and a brick-red precipitate with Fehling's solution, which are used to identify it: HCOOH + 2[Ag(NH3)2]OH -> 2Ag + CO2 + 4NH3 + 2H2O; HCOOH + 2Cu(OH)2 -> Cu2O + CO2 + 3H2O.

Ethanedioic acid, HOOC-COOH, is oxidised by acidified KMnO4 (or K2Cr2O7) to carbon dioxide and water: 2KMnO4 + 3H2SO4 + 5(COOH)2 -> K2SO4 + 2MnSO4 + 10CO2 + 8H2O. Manganese goes from +7 to +2 and carbon from +3 to +4.

blocks.alt: Three panels of equations. A, the acidic hydrogen: ethanoic acid with Na, NaOH, Na2CO3 and NaHCO3. B, replacing -OH: with SOCl2 and PCl5 to ethanoyl chloride, and esterification with ethanol. C: reduction by LiAlH4 to ethanol (not H2/Ni or NaBH4), oxidation of methanoic acid by Tollens' reagent, and oxidation of ethanedioic acid by acidified KMnO4.
blocks.caption: Reactions of carboxylic acids (original summary of the book's equations).
blocks.long_description: The acidic hydrogen is replaced by a metal to form a salt; the -OH group is replaced by Cl or by an alkoxy group; and the whole carboxyl group is reduced to CH2OH. Methanoic and ethanedioic acids are exceptions that can be oxidised further, to carbon dioxide.
